title: THE CITY THAT WALKED AHEAD OF THE SUNRISE
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: The set's widest physical canvas and a concrete, visual clock: a walking city of sixty thousand, nine days of margin, a rule that is a memorial for three thousand dead, and a canyon people the city once left behind. Both Wenna Thaw and Warden Dov Arkady are right in ways the other cannot yet hear, and the Council, Hollowers and any walker may refuse. The kind of intelligence differs again from S1 and S2 (kinematics, resonance, reading a rule as grief rather than regulation). The decisive idea, making the division the Hollowers' invitation rather than the Council's rupture, turns an old wound into the way through. A real positive result is available: the whole city across the Rift, the cisterns intact, the Rule amended by those it wounded.

R14 check before prose. Aim: get the whole city across the Rift without leaving anyone and without cracking the cisterns of Hollow Town. Counterparts: Conductor Wenna Thaw (the Rule is the only promise the city ever kept; it is a vow at a graveside, not a regulation) and Warden Dov Arkady (the city treats his people as a gap in its timetable; the cisterns were dug by the cut-loose). Strongest objection on the page: Thaw's three thousand names and Arkady's 'we have never been a place'. What Illuminara must understand: the Rule is not about distance but about nobody facing the sun alone, and the Hollowers are exactly the people who once did; the two griefs are from the same night at Marrow Pass. Care becomes action as a walk the whole length of the city, a request that each read the other's dead aloud, her refusal to carry or to vote, and one piece of physics she gives and cannot enforce (staggered footfall so the cistern walls see a hum rather than a bell). Freely chosen change: Arkady makes the invitation, Thaw answers it, the Council votes 41-19 for a clause the Left helped write; Hale among the nineteen. Concrete result: the whole city across the Rift, one hairline cistern seam repaired, Hollow Town with a Council seat and a first claim on rail hours, the dusk bell reading both ledgers. Felt moment: scene 2, walking in step, the city as one held hand. Remaining costs: eleven hundred Walkers refused the Heel half, some will not speak to Thaw, the century is not repaid, an hour of margin is gone. Open to the critic: whether scenes 4 and 5 are too articulate, whether the vote arrives too neatly, whether the hairline-crack beat lets power do too much, and whether six speake

The draft has a living centre: a Rule that turns out to be a vow at a graveside, the hum of sixty thousand people in step as one held hand, two ledgers read in the other's mouth, and a physics gift (stagger the footfall) that Illuminara can show but cannot enforce. She refuses to carry the city, to vote or to speak for either side, which is the right shape of power. The weaknesses are all in the causal middle. The mechanism that saves the cisterns is announced in one Council speech rather than found where the reader can watch; it is never tested before the crossing; the people who carry the physical risk (Hollow Town) and the people who pay the social cost (the Walkers who refuse) are named but receive no safeguard or voice; and scenes 4 and 5 restate their own meaning. None of this needs a new story. It needs the load-bearing turn dramatised and the aftermath given witnesses.

AUTHOR_REVISION by Claude (the designated author on this odd day) after the T02 fallback self-review. Protected: the Rule as a vow at a graveside, the walk in step, the two ledgers read in the other's mouth with the stumbled names, her refusal to carry, vote or speak for either side, the physics offered as something she cannot enforce, the four-minute held stone (now one pair among many), the closing child's hand and both ledgers. Added: the planted knock, the failed-and-recovered rehearsal, the rider, Hale's reason and action, one refuser's voice, the shade and margin. Outcome (3a): the whole city crosses, one seam mended, Hollow Town gains a seat, first claim on rail hours and the mending of its own water; decisive contribution is the question that sends two leaders to read each other's dead plus a piece of physics she found by attention and gave without enforcing. Remaining costs: eleven hundred refusers, seventeen leavers, Pike's silence, the century unpaid, an hour of margin gone. Speakers now six (Illuminara, Thaw, Arkady, Hale, Kesa, Pike; Pike speaks once and serves the refuser's voice). Ready for a final only after a peer or self critique of this revision.

T03 repaired what T02 named: the knock is planted in scene 3, the rehearsal fails and is recovered by people while she watches, the rider and Hale's reason exist, one refuser speaks, and the shade and margin are stated. The story's living centre is intact (the Rule as a vow at a graveside, the walk in step, the two ledgers read in the other's mouth). What remains is not structural. It is three finishing problems: the ending reports its outcome as a tally; the Council still resolves faster than its cost is paid; and the theme is still said aloud in three places, in a draft that has grown past its natural length. These can be handled inside one AUTHOR_FINAL without a further round, which matters because the 20:30 admission leaves exactly one author slot (19:30) and one close slot (20:30).

AUTHOR_FINAL by Claude (the designated author on this odd day), written in one pass at the 19:30 slot because the 20:30 admission leaves one close slot. Protected from T03/T04: the Rule as a vow at a graveside; the walk in step; the two ledgers read in the other's mouth with the stumbled names; her refusal to carry, vote or speak for either side; the physics offered as something she cannot enforce, with the knock planted in scene 3; the held stone as one pair of hands among many; Hale's recorded no and the lamp line held nine hours; Pike's refusal; the closing child's hand and both ledgers. Changed: outcome shown as things and acts; the rider priced and answered; theme spoken once. Outcome (3a): the whole city crosses, one cistern seam is mended, Hollow Town gains a seat, a first claim on rail hours and the mending of its own water; decisive contribution is the question that sends two leaders to read each other's dead plus a piece of physics found by attention and given without enforcing. Remaining costs: eleven hundred refusers, seventeen leavers, Pike's silence, a century unpaid, an hour of margin gone, nine days of thirst for Hollow Town's terraces. Speakers: six (Illuminara, Thaw, Arkady, Hale, Kesa, Pike).

final_critic_line: Illuminara learns that Orrin Kell's Rule and Hollow Town's refusal are grief held in opposite forms, then joins the two communities' freely chosen repair with one testable piece of physics, so the city crosses without being carried, the abandoned gain a permanent voice and both ledgers are heard.
